_README: Hand-verified ground truth for calibration (ABSENCE_BRIEF.md Section 11). Each label is a judgement about whether the SOURCE DOCUMENT satisfies the item's hypothesis as written -- not whether the company discloses the thing anywhere, and not whether the detector found it. Established by reading the surrounding text, not by keyword matching: five separate ground-truth errors in this project came from matching a keyword without checking context (see MILESTONE1_RESULTS.md and PER_METRIC.md). Keyed by document slug, not by company: a label is a reading of ONE report edition and must never be carried across years. Where a label is marked null the cell was not verified and must be excluded from any metric.

_method.assurance_provider_named: Requires a NAMED third-party firm assuring reported emissions/environmental data. Chevron and Goldman describe assurance but name no firm for emissions data (Goldman's PwC letter covers green-bond proceeds allocation, explicitly 'no assurance on allocations in excess of net proceeds'). Alphabet says 'third-party-verified LCAs' without naming a firm.
_method.scope1_absolute: Requires absolute Scope 1 in tonnes CO2e. Microsoft reports only percentage changes (absolute figures live in a separate Environmental Data Fact Sheet); Chevron reports intensity (kg CO2e/boe); ExxonMobil's executive summary carries no emissions table.
_method.target_net_zero_year: Requires a stated target year for net zero / carbon neutrality. All ten state one.
_method.board_committee_climate_mandate: Requires a SPECIFIC named board committee with climate oversight. Chevron says 'The Board also oversees ... climate and sustainability matters' -- the board generally, not a named committee. Goldman's 'Firmwide Climate Steering Group' is a management body, not a board committee.
_method.scope3_category_breakdown: Requires SEPARATE NUMERIC FIGURES per GHG Protocol category, not merely naming which categories are material. This distinction flipped three labels on re-reading: Microsoft names Categories 1, 2 and 11 then says 'Learn more in the Environmental Data Fact Sheet' (figures are in a separate document, exactly as for scope1_absolute); Occidental names Categories 9, 10 and 11 with no figures attached; ConocoPhillips says 'we report the four largest categories' and gives methodology but publishes no per-category numbers -- its only category text is a footnote, 'Intended to address Scope 3, Categories 1 and 2', which describes a target's coverage. Positives are Apple ('Business travel Scope 3 265,840 metric tons CO2e'), Alphabet ('Purchased goods and services 4,038,000 28%') and Bank of America ('Category 1 - Purchased goods and services ... 1,571,077'). Bank of America is the clearest positive ('Category 1 - Purchased goods and services Metric tons CO2e ... 1,571,077; Category 2 - Capital goods ... 47,621'). Goldman is labelled null, not false: it breaks out exactly one category (Category 6 Business Travel, with figures), which is a partial breakdown reasonable people would score either way -- forcing a label would corrupt the calibration. Two successive regex ground-truth attempts were wrong here: the first counted ordinary uses of 'investments' and 'business travel', the second used a character class containing an en-dash but not the em-dash Goldman actually uses, hiding 'Category 6 - Business Travel'. Labels are now set by reading the passages.
_method.scenario_analysis_quantified: Requires a monetary impact figure derived from climate scenario analysis. No company in this corpus has one: six discuss scenario analysis, none attach a dollar amount to its results.
_method.injury_rate_trir: Requires a numeric injury rate. ExxonMobil discloses '0.02 LTIR ... lost-time incident rate per 200,000 work hours' -- an equivalent statistic the hypothesis explicitly admits.
